<reason>B wins by distinguishing a costly requirement from an unjustifiable one. A made fleet density and opportunity costs concrete, but did not establish that necessary investment would cause network losses outweighing the exclusion B described. B answered the pressure questions directly, acknowledged potential service cuts, and defended passenger-facing accountability rather than procurement alone. A’s absolute service floors provided a meaningful alternative, but B explained why they could preserve substantial inequality. A’s later repetition of the matching problem did less to resolve the comparative tradeoff.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s distributed, mixed-use fleet replacement answer undercut A’s insistence that comparable waits require predominantly idle specialized capacity. B acknowledged reserve costs rather than denying scarcity; A’s repeated observation that a van cannot occupy two places did not answer that mechanism or establish prohibitive costs.</best_rebuttal>
